Impute incomplete ISO 8601 date/datetime strings

Source: R/impute_dtc.r
ks_impute_dtc.Rd

Parses truncated ISO 8601 date or datetime character strings and imputes missing components according to the chosen direction, returning a tibble with the resulting POSIXct and an imputation flag.

Usage

ks_impute_dtc(x, direction = "no", tz = "UTC", ref = NULL)

Arguments

x

Character vector of ISO 8601 truncated date/datetime strings. Accepted formats: "YYYY", "YYYY-MM", "YYYY-MM-DD", "YYYY-MM-DDTHH", "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM", "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS". A space may replace T as the date-time separator. Trailing timezone designators (Z, +HH:MM, -HH:MM) are accepted but ignored; the tz argument governs the output timezone.

direction

One of "no", "start", or "end". Controls how missing components are filled. Validated via match.arg.

tz

IANA timezone string applied to the output POSIXct values. Defaults to "UTC".

ref

NULL (default), or a Date, POSIXct, or POSIXlt reference vector recycled to length(x). When provided, missing components whose year (and optionally month) match the corresponding reference are filled from that reference rather than using the directional fallback.

Value

A tibble with one row per element of x and two columns:

dt

POSIXct in timezone tz, or NA when the year is absent or imputation could not be completed.

imputation_flag

character; the highest-priority component that was imputed: "M" (month), "D" (day), "H" (hour), "S" (minute). NA when no imputation was performed.

Details

## Parsing

Each element of x is matched against a regular expression that captures year, month, day, hour, minute, and second independently. The date-time separator may be T or a single space. Trailing timezone designators (Z, +HH:MM, -HHMM) are silently stripped; all output is placed in the timezone given by tz. Elements that do not match the pattern produce dt = NA and imputation_flag = NA.

## Completeness and imputation flags

A string is considered complete when year, month, and day are all present, and — if a time separator (T or space) is present — hour and minute are also present. Complete strings are assembled directly without imputation (flag NA), except for date-only strings under direction = "end" (Case D, see below).

The imputation_flag records the most significant component that was imputed:

FlagMeaning
"M"Month was imputed (year was the only component present).
"D"Day was imputed (year and month were present).
"H"Hour (and minute) were imputed.
"S"Minute was imputed (hour was already present).
NANo imputation was performed.

## Direction

"start"

Each missing component is filled with the earliest plausible value: month \(\to\) 1, day \(\to\) 1, hour \(\to\) 0, minute \(\to\) 0.

"end"

Each missing component is filled with the latest plausible value: month \(\to\) 12, day \(\to\) last day of that month (correctly handling leap years), hour \(\to\) 23, minute \(\to\) 59.

"no"

No imputation is performed. Incomplete strings return dt = NA and imputation_flag = NA.

## Date-only strings with a directional imputation (Cases D and E)

A date-only string such as "2020-04-06" contains no time separator and is otherwise complete. Because the time was not recorded, it is always considered imputed when direction != "no":

Case D (direction = "end")

Time is imputed as 23:59:00. Flag: "H".

Case E (direction = "start")

Time is imputed as 00:00:00. Flag: "H".

A reference-date match (Case C) overrides both Case D and Case E.

## Reference-guided imputation

When ref is provided and direction != "no", the function first checks whether the parsed year (and optionally month and day) match the corresponding reference value before applying the directional fallback. Cases are evaluated in priority order:

Case A — day missing, year + month match ref

When the day (and time) are absent but year and month equal the reference, day, hour, and minute are taken from ref. Directional start/end values are not used. Typical flag: "D".

Case B — month missing, year matches ref

When month (and therefore day and time) are absent but the year equals the reference year, month, day, hour, and minute are all taken from ref. Typical flag: "M".

Case C — date complete, time absent, full date matches ref

A date-only string whose year, month, and day all equal the reference has its time filled from ref. This takes priority over the Case D / Case E directional time fallback. Flag: "H".

Fallback

If none of Cases A–C applies — because ref is NULL, the year does not match, or the month does not match — the directional start/end values are used as described above.

ref is recycled to length(x) via rep_len(). A Date ref is coerced to POSIXct in timezone tz before its components are extracted.

Examples

# --- direction = "no" -------------------------------------------------------
# Complete datetime — no imputation, flag NA
ks_impute_dtc("2020-03-15T10:30:00", "no")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-03-15 10:30:00 NA             

# Truncated with direction = "no" — returns NA (nothing to impute)
ks_impute_dtc("2020-03", "no")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt     imputation_flag
#>   <dttm> <chr>          
#> 1 NA     NA             

# Invalid string
ks_impute_dtc("not-a-date", "no")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt     imputation_flag
#>   <dttm> <chr>          
#> 1 NA     NA             

# --- direction = "start" ----------------------------------------------------
# Year only → 2020-01-01 00:00:00, flag "M"
ks_impute_dtc("2020", "start")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-01-01 00:00:00 M              

# Year-month → first day of month, flag "D"
ks_impute_dtc("2020-03", "start")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-03-01 00:00:00 D              

# Date-only + end → end-of-day 23:59, flag "H" (Case D)
ks_impute_dtc("2020-03-15", "end")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-03-15 23:59:00 H              

# Date-only + start → midnight 00:00, flag "H" (Case E)
ks_impute_dtc("2020-03-15", "start")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-03-15 00:00:00 H              

# --- direction = "end" ------------------------------------------------------
# End of February in a leap year → 2020-02-29 23:59:00, flag "D"
ks_impute_dtc("2020-02", "end")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-02-29 23:59:00 D              

# End of March → 2020-03-31 23:59:00, flag "D"
ks_impute_dtc("2020-03", "end")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-03-31 23:59:00 D              

# --- ref: same-period guided imputation ------------------------------------
ref <- as.POSIXct("2020-03-15 10:30:00", tz = "UTC")

# Case A — day missing, year+month match ref → take day/time from ref
ks_impute_dtc("2020-03", "start", ref = ref)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-03-15 10:30:00 D              

# Case C overrides D — date matches ref → take time from ref, not 23:59
ks_impute_dtc("2020-03-15", "end", ref = ref)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-03-15 10:30:00 H              

# ref year/month mismatch → directional fallback used instead
ks_impute_dtc("2020-04", "start", ref = ref)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   dt                  imputation_flag
#>   <dttm>              <chr>          
#> 1 2020-04-01 00:00:00 D              

# --- Vectorised with dplyr::bind_cols() ------------------------------------
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(dplyr)
df <- tibble::tibble(
  dtc = c("2020-03-15T08:00", "2020-03-15", "2020-03", "2020", "bad"),
  ref = as.POSIXct(c(NA, "2020-03-15 14:30:00",
                     "2020-03-10 08:00:00", "2020-05-01 00:00:00", NA),
                   tz = "UTC")
)
dplyr::bind_cols(df, ks_impute_dtc(df$dtc, "start", ref = df$ref))
} # }
